requested_outcome: Every public discovery world offers useful truth-based sorting, while default result lists and place sliders rotate to a different stable order on each fresh browser document without changing during interaction.
natural_destination: VII public search/result pages and place recommendation sliders across vacations, events, spa, hourly rooms, attractions, trails and providers on desktop and mobile.
authorization_boundary: Implementation, tests and release-candidate preparation are authorized. Production publication remains conditional on the exact candidate passing the VII temporary-public release gate and verified production access.

lesson_bundle.reason: A cross-world change is not complete until the exact candidate is exercised across the whole affected family.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Require full family tests, a temporary public candidate, exact-version inspection and rollback evidence before a release claim.

lesson_bundle.reason: Sorting and refresh rotation are part of search ranking and URL-backed discovery state.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Require relevant ordering, honest missing-data behavior, URL persistence and result/map agreement.

lesson_bundle.reason: Equivalent result families must expose the same interaction model across worlds and viewports.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Require a world matrix and shared sorting primitives rather than one-off controls.

lesson_bundle.reason: Every visible sorting control must work in all applicable states.
lesson_bundle.acceptance_impact: Require every visible option to produce the promised order and omit unsupported comparisons.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Only vacation and event results receive sorting while spa, hourly, attractions, trails or providers remain unchanged.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Inventory every public result component and apply one shared option model with world-specific capabilities.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Automated family test names every world result component and verifies its sort control and ordering path.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Random order changes during a render, filter edit or scroll and makes the interface jump.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Generate one browser-document seed after hydration and keep it stable until a true refresh or new document.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Unit tests prove identical seed stability and different-seed rotation, while interaction tests preserve the order until refresh.

predicted_rejections.rejection: A price or popularity option is shown where the underlying world has no verified numeric signal.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Derive options from the actual inventory and keep missing numeric values last instead of inventing them.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Unsupported options are absent and missing values remain visible after verified values without fabricated numbers.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Sliders rotate but search results remain daily-static, or vice versa.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Use the same seeded ordering primitive at slider and default-result boundaries.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Tests cover shared rails plus all result families with different document seeds.

predicted_rejections.rejection: Sorting breaks URL reload, back navigation, map/list parity or existing availability priorities.
predicted_rejections.prevention: Persist explicit sorts in the URL, keep default rotation within existing eligibility/priority tiers and feed map/list from the same ordered set.
predicted_rejections.acceptance_check: Reload/back tests preserve explicit sort and map/list use identical ordered identifiers.

affected_family: Hebrew, English, Russian and French labels
desktop, mobile, list, grid and map result states
URL sort persistence and browser refresh behavior

midpoint_gate.trigger: Shared ordering utility plus one vacation result page and one DiscoveryItem world are working before expanding to the remaining worlds.
checks: A default order is stable inside one document and changes with a new seed.
An explicit price or rating sort overrides rotation and keeps unknown values last.
The URL stores an explicit sort but omits the default rotation value.

attack_questions: Can any world still render results without a sorting control?
Can a re-render or filter change reshuffle cards without a true refresh?
Can an option claim price, rating or popularity when the inventory cannot support it?
Can map and list show the same results in a different order or explicit sort disappear after reload?
Can a slider still use a fixed catalog order after a fresh browser document?
adversarial_close.natural_destination_evidence: Exact temporary public candidate opened on representative desktop and mobile result pages, refreshed twice, sorted explicitly and switched between list and map.
adversarial_close.affected_family_evidence: Automated cross-world matrix plus live representative routes for all public worlds and shared slider families.

effectiveness.baseline: Vacation and events have partial sort controls, several DiscoveryItem worlds have none, and default result rotation is mostly daily rather than per refresh.
effectiveness.target: One shared model covers every world, explicit sorts persist, and a true refresh changes the default order without interaction-time instability.
